title: Chocolate truffles
summary: A soft coconut-cream ganache rolled into rough balls and tossed in cocoa, dairy-free as written.
steps: Put both chocolates in a heatproof bowl.
Heat the coconut cream with the powdered erythritol until it just simmers, whisking to dissolve. Pour it over the chocolate and leave for 2 minutes.
Stir slowly from the centre outwards until smooth and glossy, then stir in the vanilla and salt.
Cover and refrigerate about 2 hours, until firm enough to scoop.
Scoop heaped teaspoons, roll quickly between cool palms, and drop into the cocoa to coat. Refrigerate in a covered box; bring to cool room temperature for 10 minutes before eating.
tips: If the ganache splits and looks oily, whisk in a teaspoon of warm water.
The rough, cocoa-dusted shape is the point: it is what gives truffles their name.

origin.history: Chocolate truffles are named for their resemblance to the truffle fungus: knobbly, irregular and dusted in cocoa. They are often said to have been created by a confectioner in Chambéry in the 1890s, though the story is traditional rather than documented; by the twentieth century ganache truffles were a standard of French confectionery.
